New isolated entry point: `scripts/build_ct_report.py`. It does not modify `scripts/build_report.py` or `report.html`, rerun simulations, regenerate postprocessing, or choose a model. Default output, once a real completed CT reference is explicitly selected, is `report_ct.html` plus `report_ct_receipt.json`.

```
python scripts/build_ct_report.py --check
python scripts/build_ct_report.py --output report_ct.html
```

Both require `results/reference_selection.json`, matching selected `results/summary.json`, and a completed native Athena CT case. The builder independently checks requested endpoints, accepted-step and actual SSPRK2-stage records, complete comet-probe coverage of the pointing with a light-time margin, positive finite PN summary quantities, and controller incomplete markers. A short real pilot cannot qualify as the XMM reference. A missing or stale prerequisite refuses output, preserving any existing report.

`--check` also verifies any present canonical movies. For both absolute and radial-contrast products it calls `audit_artifacts.verify_movie_receipt(..., expected_case=selection['animation_case'], require_gif=True)`: exact source/output hashes, actual frame epochs, physical UTC, completed source case and no marker extrapolation must match. Existing stale or unprovenanced movies refuse output instead of being embedded. Absent products remain explicitly pending. An explicit animation case may differ from the quantitative reference, and both names are displayed. No rendering runs inside the builder.

Optional selected-case receipts can be absent: their evidence is labeled pending instead of borrowing GLM numbers. Case/clock mismatches reject manuscript and timing comparisons; available timing-probe and final-volume hashes are checked. The time-series figure requires matching case, selected clock, CSV hash and source hashes. The movie displays its actual CT source case, geometric epochs and recorded interpolation. The default main report remains untouched. If integrating into `report.html` later, first preserve the old report as `report_glm_history.html` to retain the secondary history link.

The report covers ideal gamma-law MHD and Sun gravity, native HLLD/PLM/SSPRK2/staggered CT, the project’s exact consumer-grid Br/E boundary closure, actual forcing/calibration and held-out data, GTIs, comet-relative versus heliocentric flux, observer-arrival versus physical UTC, selected numerical/physical controls, native spacecraft and CCMC comparisons, PN-frame and conditional heavy-ion interpretation, native-field/thermal/work audits, analytic gates and literature limits, exact selected code capabilities, resource records, reproduction, requested charts/movie and secondary historical GLM links. Primary method/data URLs are embedded directly with their relevant claims.

Only selected completed CT pairs with matching physical inputs contribute to spatial/timestep qualification. Outcomes are recalculated from actual differences and registered CT targets; missing controls cannot pass. The original pointwise targets remain separate from the prospectively registered exposure-observable metrics (PN means, individual-frame means and exposure-weighted L1 differences). The latter never change the original pointwise status. Input and added-physics ranges are labeled sensitivity studies, not confidence intervals. The conclusion carries actual criterion flags and pending/failed evidence rather than a hardcoded convergence claim.

Domain, registered baseline timestep, spinup and outer-extent qualification additionally reads `validation/ct_convergence_summary.json`. Its plan, consumed helper/geometry/GTI hashes and each used case's probe/configuration/statistics/accepted trace/status hashes must match. Each used case must also pass the recorded formulation/provenance qualification, and domain pairs must pass the independent registered experiment-identity guard. The selected latitude bound and physical inputs are checked against the actual controls. A narrower domain needs its own passing comparison against the completed widest reference; retaining the widest registered domain makes no claim of narrower eligibility. Missing or failed initial-condition and outer-extent checks appear in the headline and conclusion. These baseline controls do not establish untested fine-grid temporal accuracy.

Every numerical/exposure pass and every physical comparison labeled qualified additionally requires the independent formulation/provenance and experiment-identity gates. Raw `passed` alone is insufficient; `qualified_pass`/`qualified_for_sensitivity` are checked. The outer pair, CFL, radial count and extent come from the prospective plan. Actual failed extended-domain attempts are separately read from controller/configuration/trace/log evidence and remain visible after a later control changes or passes. The two failed3.125AU cases never become completed scientific results; any passing2.3→2.85AU control qualifies only that registered extent/CFL.

Numerical qualification is explicitly separate from empirical accuracy in the lead and conclusion. Native metrics are accepted only for the selected case with current probe/configuration/statistics/metadata hashes and matching paired TSV residuals/correlation. Fixed STA hourly speed-threshold timing is derived without phase fitting. CCMC/selected PN incident-flux ratios come from the actual selected-clock summary, with no coarse value substituted for a fine case. The separate coarse cone checks retain their own scope. Density scenarios derive from the two training-instrument density medians; half/double temperature controls are broad scenarios, not those medians or statistical bounds.

The averaging table shows actual MOS1, MOS2 and PN GTI durations/means separately, plus the continuous103491s published-pointing mean. Actual GTI sums and consistency with the unchanged PN lead mean are checked. Detector seconds are not summed into elapsed time or a response-weighted combined EPIC value. Literature linkage source hashes are also checked before a current integrity claim; the partial native Brio–Wu comparison retains its method/branch limits and no retrospective accuracy threshold.

The live resources section uses `monitoring/latest.json`, `monitoring/start.json` and the last complete record in `monitoring/token_snapshots.jsonl`. It displays sample UTC, elapsed wall hours at that sample, available system memory, sampled matched-process RSS, shared-GPU context, planning progress and the latest note-change interval. Token usage is explicitly the tool-reported goal counter, not billing usage or an independently reconciled agent sum. CT uses CPU only; global GPU activity is not attributed to CT. Polling gaps, missed short processes and between-poll peaks are stated. The new `monitoring/summary.json` GNU-time schema is verified separately against each listed run receipt and CPU/wall/RSS aggregates, including retained failures. A newer qualifying receipt absent from a dated summary triggers a coverage warning. Legacy GLM summaries cannot masquerade as this schema and retain their original separate scope; no complete all-project CPU total is asserted.

The registered refinement-history tables are separate from selected pointwise/exposure tables. All original and additional registered pairs retain explicit selected/non-selected roles; missing additions appear as pending. Actual theta16-to32 pointwise/frame failures and the theta32 radial pair's pointwise pass with PN-total/frame failures remain visible after further refinement. Only explicitly selected actual pairs determine the selected criterion flags; untriggered conditional resolutions are not invented as required comparisons.

`checks.py` qualifies twelve guard paths against real archived artifacts: missing selection, completed GLM rejection, unrun CT rejection, real short-CT coverage rejection, explicit incomplete-marker precedence, incorrect actual stage epochs, malformed optional/required records, exclusion of historical GLM passes, missing temporal controls, and missing exposure metrics without mutating pointwise flags. It creates no scientific preview HTML or invented model values. Protected root report/postprocessing files are hash-checked around the test. `verification.json` records the builder hash and this scope.

`control_checks.py` exercises the actual independent control receipt with in-memory metadata perturbations: missing evidence, wrong plan hash, outside-results serial preview, wrong clock and stale helper provenance cannot qualify a control. It checks the actual latest token-counter parsing. Once a completed wider-domain pair exists it also tests probe-hash and unregistered-target rejection against that real pair. `control_verification.json` explicitly records any guards still awaiting a completed pair. No scientific preview is generated.

`feature_checks.py` adds24 actual-data guards: selected native/correlation/timing checks and stale or invented metric rejection; actual per-detector/continuous averages; retained failed outer runs; dynamically registered-pair substitution rejection; qualified spatial and physical controls; current literature linkage and stale-source rejection; both actual41frame movie receipts and isolated source/output/case/GIF/provenance negatives. It computes fixtures from existing outputs only, writes no selection or scientific HTML, and verifies protected main-report/history/postprocessing/renderer files remain unchanged.

`refinement_checks.py` adds12 actual-data history/cost guards: dynamically added coordinate pairs, both observed refinement-failure modes, separation of selected criteria, pending new pairs, no invented contingent resolutions, actual failed-run GNU-time inclusion, aggregate/hash failures, omitted-receipt coverage and legacy-schema rejection. The combined qualification currently contains59 passing guards across four verification receipts. No model run, final reference selection or report rendering is part of these tests.

At qualification time no completed CT production case was explicitly selected. Full scientific HTML rendering is therefore intentionally pending a real final reference and regenerated products. The builder's refusal is part of its tested behavior, not a preview report. Once root selects a completed CT case, rerun `--check`, the actual renderer, and the artifact audit for final integration.
